name: Text File Encoding Converter
description: Convert text files between UTF-8 and UTF-16 with live preview, then re-save with the correct encoding and optional BOM.
body:
Preview

Load a text file to preview its contents and conversion.
howto: Load a text file with the file picker.
Confirm the source encoding — the tool auto-detects UTF-8 vs UTF-16 from the BOM or content.
Choose the target encoding and whether to include a BOM.
Review the preview panel to confirm the text looks right.
Click Convert & download to save the re-encoded file.
features: Auto-detection of UTF-8 and UTF-16 from BOM
Convert between UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE and Latin-1

faq.a: A file saved in UTF-16 can look like a wall of garbage in a UTF-8 reader and vice versa. Correct encoding ensures the text displays and imports cleanly everywhere.
The byte-order mark is a small marker at the start of a text file that tells readers which encoding and byte order was used. Windows tools often expect it.

faq.q: Can I convert a .docx or binary file?
faq.a: No — this tool is for plain text files (.txt, .csv, .json, .md, config files and similar). Binary formats need their own converters.
No. Conversion uses the browser's TextDecoder/TextEncoder and Blob API entirely on your device.
